name: Executive order of September 21, 1880 setting apart a reservation for the Jicarilla Apache
aka: First Jicarilla reservation west of the Tierra Amarilla grant
promises: This was an executive order, not a treaty. The President set apart a reserve for the Jicarilla from the southwest corner of the Tierra Amarilla grant north to the Colorado line, west 16 miles, south, and back east (Royce area 624). The Commission describes it as a rectangular reserve of 480 square miles.
landTaken: None by this order. Royce records that the order was revoked and the land restored to the public domain by executive order of May 15, 1884, and that a reservation with some differences of boundary was set apart again in 1887.
compensation: None for this reserve as such. The Jicarilla aboriginal land claim (Docket 22-A) ended in a stipulated final award of $9,150,000 on April 21, 1971.
today: The Indian Claims Commission held that the United States took the Jicarilla's Indian title without compensation on August 20, 1883, when the Army began removing them to Fort Stanton, and treated the earlier reservation attempts as brief and unsuccessful. It found the 1887 reservation, where they have lived since, virtually the same as the one created by the 1880 order. That taking is recorded under cession-1886-10-01-apache-eastern-bands and is not counted again here.

openQuestions: The revocation of this reserve (Royce: executive order of May 15, 1884; Commission Finding 55: restored to the public domain in August 1883; Commission opinion: returned to the public domain in 1884) is not counted as a breach under the rule for executive-order land, and the Commission's finding dates the taking to the 1883 removal, not to the revocation.
The 1887 order is dated February 1, 1887 in Finding 56 and February 11, 1887 in the 1966 opinion; Royce's scan is unclear. Not used in the record.
Whether the 1880 reserve lay wholly inside the Commission's Finding 60 area was not plotted.
The Jicarilla Apache Nation's own account of the 1880 reservation was not located.

Audit 2026-11-08: Royce pp. 902-903 and 925 and Docket 22-A (OSU 746 Findings 55-56, 1536, 2436, 2037) reopened: 480 square miles, the August 20, 1883 taking, "virtually the same" 1887 reservation and the stipulated $9,150,000 award of April 21, 1971 confirmed. Royce's scan gives the 1887 order as Feb. 14, 1887, a third date; still not used.
